Subject: Recap + next steps: HIPAA / BAA eligibility for MedCare Health

Hi Tom — thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our call with Amanda: 

Summary of requirements we heard:
- MedCare will need a Business Associate Agreement (BAA) before you route PHI to any vendor.
- Use case will involve clinical notes and patient identifiers (so this is PHI under HIPAA).
- Preferred deployment options: you mentioned a preference for an environment where MedCare controls keys and logging (you said "private environment if possible").

Quick answers & what we can provide: 
- Redwood is SOC 2 Type II compliant; we can share a redacted SOC 2 report for your review.
- BAAs are supported — we typically provide BAAs for Dedicated (reserved capacity) and Private (VPC / on-prem) deployments.
- Public hosted multi-tenant API is generally not eligible for PHI processing unless a customer-specific isolation/contract arrangement is in place; for MedCare's requirements we anticipate Dedicated or Private will be the right fit.
- For Dedicated/Private we can support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM), extended audit logs, and configurable data retention.

Next steps we propose: 
1) I'm attaching the initial vendor security questionnaire you mentioned — please fill and return when convenient (MedCare_Vendor_Security_Questionnaire.pdf).
2) Neha (cc'd) will follow up with SOC 2 evidence and a draft BAA for your legal team to review.
3) We'll schedule a short session with Dylan (solutions engineer) to walk through deployment options and PHI boundaries if you'd like — available early next week.

Let me know if that aligns with your expectations or if there are other stakeholders we should loop in.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole

Thanks Marissa — that recap is right on. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Confirmed: MedCare will be sending clinical notes and patient identifiers to the model as part of a summarization workflow — that is definitely PHI.
- BAA: required before any production processing of PHI. Happy to review your draft.
- Deployment: our Security & Compliance team prefers Private (VPC/on-prem) for initial rollout. If Dedicated can provide equivalent network isolation and customer-managed keys, we can consider that as well — need to confirm with our infra team.
- Timeline: We're aiming for a pilot in Q3; legal will want SOC 2 and the BAA in the next 2-3 weeks to stay on schedule.

Can you also confirm whether Redwood supports customer-managed KMS keys for Dedicated? That will be a gating item for us.

Appreciate the quick follow-up.
—Tom

From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>

Hi Tom / team — thanks for the clear notes. Quick answers from Redwood Security & Privacy below, plus attachments: redacted SOC 2 report and our standard BAA draft with commentary.

1) SOC 2: Redwood completed SOC 2 Type II in 2026. Redacted report attached (SOC2_Report_Redacted.pdf). If you need an NDA / mutual non-disclosure before receiving the full report, we can do that — let me know.

2) BAA availability: we provide BAAs for Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) and Private deployments (VPC or on-prem). Our standard hosted multi-tenant API is not eligible for processing PHI in production due to shared tenancy; exceptions require a commercial isolation agreement and separate contract negotiation.

3) PHI handling / key management: 
- Dedicated: supports customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own-key) for model inputs/outputs at rest and keys for any persisted artifacts. Audit logging is available with per-request identifiers.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): full control of networking and keys; recommended for highest compliance needs.
- Hosted API: allowed for non-PHI or de-identified data only.

4) Data retention & telemetry: default ephemeral caches are enabled for performance; for PHI workloads we recommend disabling persistent prefix caching and enabling strict retention policies. We can document what telemetry is retained (request metadata, timestamps, per-token logs, and debug traces when enabled) and provide configuration options.

5) Next steps / timeline: 
- I'll attach the BAA draft (BAA_Draft_Redlines.docx) for your legal team to review.
- Please send back the completed vendor questionnaire; we'll mark priority once we have it.
- If MedCare confirms Dedicated is acceptable we can scope capacity and security controls this week; otherwise we can plan for Private deployment onboarding which has longer lead time (infrastructure scheduling).

Happy to jump on a 30-minute call with your infra and legal teams to run through the BAA and KMS details — proposed slots on Tue/Wed next week.

Best,
